missionFit.rule: Cover consequential credit-union industry developments with a concrete, source-supported implication for CU decision makers. AI and technology remain signature strengths, not mandatory angles. Material regulation, finance, lending, payments, member service, workforce, competition and governance qualify without an invented AI connection. Reject routine personnel notices, promotion-only releases and generic developments without meaningful CU consequence.
examplesInScope: payments, identity, cybersecurity and data technology
AI workforce, vendor and compliance implementation
Material CU regulation, financial performance, consolidation and member-impact developments without a technology angle
Official model and workplace-AI changes with verified availability and a concrete CU implication

productionBehavior: Candidates that pass hard stops and score at or above the minimum proceed through the existing exact-head PR checks and authorized release path. The same publisher verifies production and reconciles canonical state through the permitted checkout-capable preservation path. Failed candidates are logged with reasons and do not request routine human approval.

statePersistence.rule: After the article package has persisted the dated daily-cycle outcome, a connector-only runtime must not perform a second whole-file replacement merely to finalize deployment or social fields. Treat automation/social-queue.json and the coverage ledger as authoritative for final distribution truth. If daily-cycle reconciliation is still useful, defer it to a checkout-capable, history-preserving path that runs scripts/validate-daily-cycle-preservation.mjs against current main and re-fetches the committed blob for strict UTF-8/JSON and preservation verification.
statePersistence.reason: The September 9 and September 14 secondary finalization writes corrupted the append-style daily-cycle ledger despite the primary publication outcome already being safely persisted.

cycleOwnership.articleCycle: Owns News and Insights only: target three distinct qualified articles per weekday, maximum three, through the same sequential daily publisher and unchanged schedule. Fifteen per full week is a target, not a guarantee or minimum output obligation. No weekend cycle or retrospective filling of closed days. No Alerts. Never extend bounded research or weaken gates to fill slots.
cycleOwnership.alertCycle: Owns Alerts separately under automation/scheduled-tasks/cuai-operating-system.md. It may publish at most one genuinely new, time-sensitive, qualified Alert per weekday and has no quota or minimum target. Any legacy alert target count in daily-cycle-state.json is non-authoritative metadata and must not drive publication behavior.

standardCycle.completionRule: Prospectively after release, use fullArticleTargetByWeekday for the Eastern date in the next ordinary weekday cycle; never reopen a completed cycle to fill the new target. Each article independently passes all gates, uses a distinct event and preferably different beat/format, and is committed and production-verified sequentially before starting the next package. Stop at three, an unresolved technical/permission gate, or exhaustion of the same bounded candidate pool and approved fallbacks. Preserve every earlier same-day publication, exact validation receipt and count. Alerts and social caps remain separate and unchanged.
standardCycle.shortfallRule: Never weaken evidence, mission-fit or quality gates to fill a slot. Record each unfilled slot in regularPublicationSlots with its actual editorial/approval hold or owned technical checkpoint/blocker, explicit reason and bounded next action. Record candidates evaluated, rejection reasons, beats/sources and exact evidence gaps. Do not invent run identities or label a technical block an editorial hold. Fifteen per full week is not a mandatory minimum; siteStoriesMin is legacy target metadata. The separate Alert cycle has no quota.

expansionReview.activation: Next ordinary weekday cycle after an authorized release; private preparation is not activation. No retroactive filling of closed cycles.
expansionReview.target: 15 qualified articles per full week; partial weeks and explicit held slots are not an obligation to backfill
expansionReview.formatRule: Aim for at least three formats and five functions per week. At most two framework/checklist articles combined per week absent a recorded material-news exception. No rigid topic quota and no padding.
expansionReview.nextStage: Any further volume increase requires a new owner decision; no automatic escalation.
expansionReview.continueCriteria: Review actual qualified output, held and failed slots, corrections, breadth, production correctness, existing usage and available engagement after two completed weeks. Do not infer capacity or source supply from synthetic tests. No new recurring spend.
expansionReview.stopOrRevise: Stop later packages on unresolved material sourcing/deployment failures, permission blocks or exhausted existing usage; preserve all completed packages and owned checkpoints. Record explicit reasons for unfilled slots, diagnose repeated capacity/source shortfalls, and never add scans, spend, schedules or weaker gates to fill the target.
